rules.reason: This call sends the fetched secret itself into a file, a dump command (head/cat/base64/tee/...) or a network tool — how a token leaked before. A fetch may share a call with other commands; capture it instead: TOKEN=$(wf secret get KEY --backend bitwarden), and use $TOKEN only in a header or argument, never printed, redirected or piped.

wf secret env prints every resolved secret value at once — redirected to a file, piped into a dump or network command, or followed by an environment listing (printenv, env, set, export -p) or a secret-named variable printed into one, this is a whole-credential-set leak. Use `eval "$(wf secret env ...)"` and read single variables in headers only.

Same leak shape as `wf secret get` (see docs/solutions/security/wf-secrets-default-backend-and-redaction-pitfalls.md) — capture into a shell variable; the value itself must never be redirected to a file, piped into a dump or network command, or printed from its variable.

bws secret list --output json includes the raw `value` field for every secret in scope — piping it straight into a dump or network command or redirecting it to a file exposes all of them at once. Filter it with jq to key/projectId/len(value)/revisionDate only, as documented.

bws secret edit/create/get echo the FULL secret back, including the value you just set — dumping that response leaks it. This happened: a rotation printed its replacement and had to be redone. Redirect to a file; print only key/revisionDate/len(value).

This dump command is fed a real secret (wf secret get/env, bws secret get/list, or a variable captured from one) by a pipe, here-string or process substitution — dumping the value is how a secret leaked before. Dumping anything else in the same call is fine; drop the secret from this command.

A real secret value (wf secret get/env, bws secret get/list, or a variable captured from one) is piped or here-stringed into this network tool as its input — that sends the secret off-box. Using a captured variable inside a header or argument (curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN") is allowed.
git commit --no-verify is not allowed - it skips lefthook (lint/format). Fix the issues instead; the documented kill-switch is for humans outside the agent.

git push --no-verify is not allowed - it skips the pre-push gate (`wf check --pushed`: the typecheck, lint, unit and flow tests CI would run, through the shared Nx cache). Run them and fix what is red; the documented kill-switch is for humans outside the agent.
gh api mutations (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) are not allowed. Use read-only GET requests only.
git checkout --force discards uncommitted changes. Use 'git stash' first.
git checkout -- discards uncommitted working tree changes permanently. Use 'git stash' first.
git checkout --pathspec-from-file can overwrite multiple files. Use 'git stash' first.
git switch --discard-changes/--force discards uncommitted changes. Use 'git stash' first.
git restore --worktree explicitly discards working tree changes. Use 'git stash' first.
git reset --hard/--merge destroys uncommitted changes permanently. Use 'git stash' first.
git clean -f removes untracked files permanently. Use 'git clean -n' to preview first.
git push --force destroys remote history. Use --force-with-lease for safer force push.
git branch -D force-deletes without merge check. Use -d for safe delete.
git worktree remove --force can delete uncommitted changes. Remove --force flag.
find -delete permanently removes files. Use -print first to preview.
find -exec rm is dangerous. Use -print first to preview the file list.
xargs rm/find with dynamic stdin input is dangerous. Use an explicit file list instead.
parallel rm/shell with dynamic input is dangerous. Use an explicit file list instead.

Documentation lives under the root docs/ folder. Do not create or edit docs/ folders inside apps, packages, features, scripts, .agents, patches, or other non-root locations.

Production images are built by CI (a push to dev: the build-image action on the runner), not here: the VM is arm64 and a local build emulates and eats the sandbox disk. A hand build runs in agent-shell's own docker, never into a production tag.
Starting a local Docker daemon is only ever the first step of a local image build, which this repo does on the VM instead -- see the `docker build` rule. Use `wf vm exec` against the VM's own daemon.
